newsitem.title: UK: UK budget taxes dividends on trading asset shares.
newsitem.headline: UK budget taxes dividends on trading asset shares.

text.p: British-based firms which deal in shares will have to pay tax on the dividends as a result of Wednesday's budget in a move aimed at countering dividend buying by dealers.

The change, whereby "dividends on shares which are trading assets will themselves be treated as part of the holder's trading profits", came into effect immediately and the Labour government expects it to yield nearly 500 million stg to April 2001.

But Labour's first budget since 1978 stressed those who hold shares as investments would not be affected by the measure, which supersedes previous rules under which only certain dividends on such shares were treated as part of the trading profits.
It said the measures meant dividends on UK equities could, on the whole, be taken outside the scope of the provision.
"Changes have been made so that in future this provision will apply mainly to transactions in overseas equities by dealers," it added.
But the government also warned firms against taking measures to avoid the tax.

"If the government has reason to think that this yield is being reduced by moving shares into the hands of associates for whom they are not trading assets, it will take action to block such manoeuvres," it said.
Any such action would take effect from the introduction of the new rules, it added.
